newsitem.title: SAO TOME AND PRINCIPE: Sao Tome President names new prime minister.
newsitem.headline: Sao Tome President names new prime minister.

text.p: The President of the African twin island state of Sao Tome and Principe, Miguel Trovoada, named a new prime minister on Tuesday following the collapse of the islands' coalition government.

Trovoada named Raul Braganca, deputy leader of the Movement for the Liberation of Sao Tome and Principe/Social Democratic Party (MLSTP/PSD), to replace Armindo Vaz de Almeida as head of government after two months of political talks.

Braganca, an army major in his 60s who served twice as defence minister in the one-party state that ruled Sao Tome from 1975 until 1991, is seen as a consensus figure who has not been tainted by recent corruption scandals.
Braganca will head a coalition government with his party and the Party of Democratic Convergence (PCD).
Both parties voted to bring down the previous government on September 20 because of what they called "bad management, inefficiency, incapacity and corruption."

The new coalition faces spiralling inflation and increasing social unrest in the impoverished islands of 127,000 people, which have been hit by a wave of strikes by health workers, teachers and civil servants in recent months.
